stem.text: The amount of sand in a pile, measured in cubic feet, is modeled by a twice-differentiable function S of time t, measured in hours. It is known that \( S''(6) = -2 \). Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( S''(6) = -2 \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: At time t = 6 hours, the rate at which the amount of sand in the pile is changing is decreasing at a rate of 2 cubic feet per hour per hour.

worked_solution.text: \( S''(6) \) is the rate of change of \( S' \), the rate at which the amount of sand in the pile changes, so it is measured in cubic feet per hour per hour.
worked_solution.rule_named: second derivative as the rate of change of a rate

worked_solution.text: The value is negative, so at t = 6 the rate of change of the amount of sand in the pile is itself decreasing, by 2 cubic feet per hour for each hour.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the second derivative gives the direction of change of the rate

options.label: At time t = 6 hours, the rate at which the amount of sand in the pile is changing is increasing at a rate of 2 cubic feet per hour per hour.
options.derivation: the negative value reported as a magnitude and described as an increase

options.label: At time t = 6 hours, the rate at which the amount of sand in the pile is changing is decreasing at a rate of 2 cubic feet per hour.
options.derivation: the units of the first derivative given for a rate of a rate, one time unit short

options.label: At time t = 6 hours, the amount of sand in the pile is decreasing at a rate of 2 cubic feet per hour per hour.
